title: Pia Dandiya Wins Florida Seat, Becomes Second Indian American Woman in House
excerpt: The 39-year-old former educator and White House Fellow defeated Republican Casey Askar with 51.9 per cent of the vote in Florida's redrawn 22nd District on November 3.
body:
• Pia Dandiya, 39, a Democrat whose parents immigrated from Jaipur, defeated Republican Casey Askar on November 3 to win Florida's 22nd Congressional District with 51.9 per cent of the vote.
  • She is the second Indian American woman elected to the US House of Representatives, after Pramila Jayapal, according to Punjab Outlook, and won elected office on her first attempt.
  • A former Teach For America teacher, she became founding principal of a Harlem high school at 28 and served as a 2020–2021 White House Fellow at the US Department of Education.
  • She takes office for a two-year term on January 3, 2027, succeeding Lois Frankel in the redrawn district; for diaspora readers, her win adds an Indian American woman to the House from a district with a Republican registration advantage.

Pia Dandiya is headed to Congress. The Palm Beach County native defeated Republican Casey Askar on Tuesday, November 3, to win Florida's 22nd Congressional District after a mid-decade redraw made the district more favourable to her Republican rival, according to The Palm Beach Post. She received 51.9 per cent of the vote, Punjab Outlook reported, making her the second Indian American woman elected to the US House of Representatives after Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal, who also secured re-election and welcomed Dandiya's victory.

The win came in her first bid for elected office, in a district where Republicans traditionally held an advantage in voter registration. She had won the Democratic primary in August with nearly 69 per cent of the vote. Cook Political Report rated the contest a toss-up. In her first interview with an Indian news outlet after the victory, reported by The CSR Journal, Dandiya described the first six days after the election as a whirlwind and said walking through the Capitol felt surreal, the result of 18 months of hard work.

"I started off on this journey to fight for a future worthy of my students, and worthy of my son, because every child deserves the future that we dream for our own."

— Pia Dandiya, in her November 3 victory speech, as reported by The Palm Beach Post

From a Harlem classroom to the House

Dandiya, 39, was born and raised in Jupiter, in Palm Beach County, to parents who immigrated from Jaipur in the 1980s; her father, Dr Rohit Dandiya, established a medical practice in the United States, and her mother founded a Montessori school, Punjab Outlook reported. She studied government at Harvard University and earned a master's degree in education from Boston University.

She started her career as a Teach For America corps member, teaching middle school mathematics in Boston before moving into teacher leadership development in New York. At 28, she became the founding principal of Democracy Prep Endurance High School, a public charter school in Harlem. Her work in education then took her to Washington, where she was selected for the 2020–2021 class of White House Fellows and assigned to the US Department of Education; Punjab Outlook reported she also served on President Joe Biden's Domestic Policy Council and later led public-sector initiatives at Apple.

Politics came late. According to The Palm Beach Post, Dandiya was first suggested as a potential candidate in 2019 and set the idea aside; it was President Donald Trump's victory in November 2024 that marked the turning point in her thinking about running. "Trump was elected in the fall, and that's when [Dandiya] was like, 'This is crazy. I'm going to run,'" Emily Cherniack, founder of New Politics, told the Post.

What she campaigned on

Her platform centred on lowering the cost of living, protecting Social Security and Medicare, improving education and addressing government corruption, with healthcare and gun safety also prominent, both outlets reported. Dandiya, who identifies as a centrist Democrat, eschewed what she called "extremism and performative politics" in her candidate questionnaire. "I want to work with anyone, even across the aisle, who is committed to solving problems," she told the Post.

Speaking to The CSR Journal, she also addressed anti-Indian sentiment in the United States, spoke about protecting the legacy of the Indian-American community, and urged Indian-American women not to wait for external validation before pursuing political ambitions. Her victory was celebrated by relatives in Jaipur, whom she connected with over video calls, the Journal reported.

Dandiya will serve a two-year term representing a district stretching across portions of Palm Beach, Broward, Hendry and Collier counties, according to The Palm Beach Post. She is due to take office on January 3, 2027.
